name: Cohort Analysis Checklist
description: This module is a pre-completion checklist for cohort analysis work: a short set of checks to run before calling a cohort analysis task done.
content:
This module is a pre-completion checklist for cohort analysis work: a short set of checks to run before calling a cohort analysis task done.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Document any non-obvious cohort analysis decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
2. Surface known limitations of a chosen cohort analysis approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
3. When cohort analysis decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
4. Re-check edge cases relevant to cohort analysis (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
5. When multiple cohort analysis strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
6. Prefer explicit, readable cohort analysis solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
7. When cohort analysis guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
8. Validate cohort analysis outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
9. Keep cohort analysis changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
10. Measure before optimizing any cohort analysis bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
11. State assumptions about cohort analysis explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
12. Prefer the simplest cohort analysis approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not silently drop cohort analysis edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Do not apply generic cohort analysis advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of cohort analysis correctness.
- Avoid introducing new cohort analysis abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.

CLOSING NOTE
When in doubt, prefer clarity and explicit reasoning about cohort analysis over a shortcut that saves a few lines but hides intent.
